what_it_is.prose: MRSAM (Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile) is the Indo-Israeli co-developed air defence system based on the Barak-8 missile family. The system was jointly developed by DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), with BEL and BDL as Indian production agencies. The naval variant is designated LR-SAM (Long Range Surface-to-Air Missile) and equips the Indian Navy's Kolkata-class (P15A), Visakhapatnam-class (P15B), and Nilgiri-class (P17A) destroyers and frigates. The land-based MRSAM variant is in service with the Indian Army and Indian Air Force. The missile has a range of 70-100 km (depending on variant) and an altitude ceiling of 16 km, with an active radar seeker providing end-game homing. Aggregate orders across the three services exceed ₹6,000 crore. The co-development model provides Transfer of Technology for Indian production, with the active radar seeker being progressively indigenised. MRSAM provides medium-layer air defence complementing the longer-range S-400 (India context) and the shorter-range Akash and QRSAM systems.

deployments_procurement.summary: MRSAM/LR-SAM is in operational service across all three Indian services. The naval LR-SAM variant equips Kolkata-class (P15A), Visakhapatnam-class (P15B), and Nilgiri-class (P17A) destroyers and frigates. The land-based MRSAM is in service with the Indian Army and IAF. Aggregate orders across all three services exceed ₹6,000 crore.

faq.question: What is the difference between MRSAM and LR-SAM?
faq.answer: MRSAM (Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile) is the land-based variant for the Indian Army and IAF. LR-SAM (Long Range Surface-to-Air Missile) is the naval variant that equips Indian Navy destroyers and frigates — specifically the Kolkata-class (P15A), Visakhapatnam-class (P15B), and Nilgiri-class (P17A). Both are based on the Indo-Israeli Barak-8 missile family co-developed by DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), with BEL and BDL as Indian production agencies.

faq.question: Which Indian Navy ships carry the LR-SAM?
faq.answer: LR-SAM (Barak-8) equips the Kolkata-class (P15A: INS Kolkata, INS Kochi, INS Chennai), the Visakhapatnam-class (P15B: INS Visakhapatnam, INS Mormugao, INS Imphal, INS Surat — all commissioned 2021-2024), and the Nilgiri-class (P17A: 7 frigates under construction at MDL and GRSE, first delivery 2025). Aggregate orders across all three services exceed ₹6,000 crore.

faq.question: Is the MRSAM seeker indigenous?
faq.answer: The MRSAM active radar seeker is co-developed by IAI and DRDO under a Transfer of Technology framework, with BEL and BDL producing the missile in India. The seeker is being progressively indigenised, but specific percentages are not publicly disclosed. FPGA and GaN T/R modules for the radar subsystems are industry-typically imported from the United States.
